subject.title: fix(infra): bound gateway TLS file reads via secret-file helper

question: Should gateway TLS permanently fail startup above 64 KiB for certificate/key files and 256 KiB for CA bundles while retaining the current symlink and hardlink compatibility behavior?
rationale: The bounded-read mechanism is technically sound, but choosing unconditional limits changes a shipped startup contract and balances memory hardening against valid existing certificate-chain and trust-bundle layouts.

options.title: Approve and document current caps
options.body: Adopt 64 KiB for certificate/key files and 256 KiB for CA bundles as the permanent contract, document the limits and startup error, and retain the current regression proof.

options.title: Choose larger bounded limits
options.body: Keep the same pinned helper but increase one or more caps to reduce upgrade breakage while still preventing unbounded allocation.

options.title: Pause unconditional enforcement
options.body: Do not merge until maintainers define a different compatibility or migration strategy for existing oversized TLS material.

recommendation.title: Approve and document current caps
recommendation.body: Adopt 64 KiB for certificate/key files and 256 KiB for CA bundles as the permanent contract, document the limits and startup error, and retain the current regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The gateway TLS feature and its early security contract trace most directly to this owner.
